chunks: By this sanad/isnad, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from al-Sindī, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

No servant makes faith in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sincere for forty days — or he said: no servant beautifies the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for forty days — except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, makes him abstinent regarding the world, shows him its illness and its remedy, establishes wisdom in his heart, and causes his tongue to speak by it.
Then he recited: “Indeed, those who took the calf shall be reached by wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world; and thus do We recompense the fabricators.”

So you do not see an adherent of bidʿah except humiliated, and a fabricator against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and against His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله), and against the People of his House (صلوات الله عليهم), except humiliated.

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life, viewed here as something to become detached from
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: faith in Allah in a sincere and purified sense
key_terms.الْحِكْمَةَ: wisdom that Allah establishes in the believer’s heart
key_terms.الْمُفْتَرِينَ: those who fabricate lies, especially against Allah
key_terms.بِدْعَةٍ: religious innovation that departs from truth
key_terms.دَاءَهَا: its illness, meaning the spiritual harms of worldly attachment
key_terms.دَوَاءَهَا: its remedy, meaning the cure for the harms of the worldly life
key_terms.ذِكْرَ: remembrance of Allah through sustained devotional recollection

ai.seo_question: How does forty days of sincere faith and dhikr affect the believer according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that sincere iman and sustained dhikr for forty days lead to detachment from the dunya, insight into its harms and remedies, and the rooting of wisdom in the heart. It then cites a Qur'anic verse to show that false invention against Allah is accompanied by humiliation, linking bidʿah and fabrication to spiritual disgrace.
